definitions.durSec: scene length in seconds: real cue times for subtitles, a share of the film's running time for screenplays, a reading-rate estimate otherwise
definitions.turnsPerMin: spoken turns per minute of scene
definitions.wordsP50: median words per spoken turn in the scene
definitions.wordsP90: 90th percentile of words per spoken turn in the scene
definitions.shortShare: share of turns of 5 words or fewer
definitions.microShare: share of turns of 2 words or fewer
definitions.interruptShare: share of turns that end cut off by a dash
definitions.ellipsisShare: share of turns that trail off in an ellipsis
definitions.silentTurnShare: share of turns that are only dots or a dash (a written silence)
definitions.pauseMarkersPer100: written pause markers (pause/beat/silence in a direction, or a silent turn) per 100 turns
definitions.overlapShare: timed: share of turns that start before the previous one ends
definitions.rapidShare: timed: share of turns that follow the previous one within 0.25 s (back-to-back, including a dash-split cue)
definitions.silenceShare: timed: share of the scene's span in which nobody is talking
definitions.gapsOver2sPerMin: timed: pauses longer than 2 s per minute
definitions.medianGapSec: timed: median gap between turns, seconds
definitions.longestGapFrac: timed: longest gap as a share of the scene span
definitions.wordsPerSec: timed: words spoken per second of actual speech
definitions.dirPerTurn: stage directions / action lines per spoken turn
definitions.dirPerMin: stage directions / action lines per minute
definitions.actsPerMin: directions that carry a body act (hard or soft) per minute
definitions.hardActs: directions with a hard physical act (strike, shove, grab, kill, collapse, kiss, embrace) in the scene
definitions.dialogueShare: spoken words as a share of spoken plus direction words
definitions.directionGapP50: median number of spoken turns between two directions
definitions.peak: highest smoothed conflict intensity (0-1 proxy from hostile words, shouting, cut-off lines, hard acts)
definitions.peakRise: peak intensity minus the opening level
definitions.tInciting: when intensity first reaches 40% of its rise to the peak, as a fraction of scene time (scenes with an arc only)
definitions.tClimax: when intensity peaks, as a fraction of scene time (scenes with an arc only)
definitions.aftermathShare: scene time after intensity last stays above 70% of its rise (scenes with an arc only)
definitions.reversals: turning points of the smoothed intensity with a swing of 0.12 or more (a rise then a fall is one)
definitions.eventsPer10: reveals + accusations + commitments + hard acts + reversals per 10 turns
definitions.longestQuietFrac: longest run of turns with no reveal, accusation, commitment or hard act, as a share of turns
definitions.perSource.turnsPerMin: spoken turns per minute over the whole source
definitions.perSource.sceneMinP50: median scene length in minutes (real for subtitles; see calibration for the others)
definitions.perSource.scenesPer10Min: scenes per 10 minutes (subtitle scenes are cut at 12 s of silence)
definitions.perSource.dialogueShare: spoken words / (spoken + direction words), whole source
definitions.perSource.hardActsPer10Min: hard physical acts in directions per 10 minutes
definitions.perSource.talkShare: subtitle files: share of the span with someone talking
definitions.perSource.gaps2PerMin: subtitle files: gaps over 2 s per minute (all gaps, not cut by scene)
definitions.perSource.gaps5PerMin: subtitle files: gaps over 5 s per minute
definitions.perSource.gaps12PerMin: subtitle files: gaps over 12 s per minute (these are the scene cuts)

handCheck.method: One reader (the builder, not independent) read the first 34 events of each sampled scene with its inciting beat, climax and per-turn intensity, and judged segmentation and climax placement. Two rounds: round 1 (34 scenes) found defects that were fixed; round 2 is 38 fresh scenes (seed 21) after the fixes, 6 per form (4 for the pt screenplays).

defectsFixedAfter: a speaker name cut at a title's full stop and read as shouting
kisses and embraces read as conflict
plateau peaks resolved to the last point
page furniture and watermarks in screenplay directions
stage directions glued to the front of a line

defectsSeenAfter: shooting scripts whose scene numbers are cues (dropped, 3.8% of scenes)
transcripts with no scene marks give 100+ turn scenes (capped at 120, fixed)

handCheck.reading: Climax placement is plausible in about 60% of scenes that have an arc but in 16 of 18 (89%) of strong-arc scenes (peak 0.3+, rise 0.15+). Use the strongArc ladders for tInciting, tClimax and aftermathShare. Scenes with a weak peak place the climax arbitrarily.

taggedBeats.note: Intensity proxy and act lexicon against the existing model-tagged beats of the 45 plays (labels are about 97% exact on action_type, 65% on emotion).

knownLimits: Conflict intensity is a lexicon-and-punctuation proxy. It sees open hostility, shouting and hard acts, not subtext, coldness or fear; against the hot-emotion tags it is barely above chance (AUC 0.56) and against violent action it is good (AUC 0.85).
Subtitle figures come from cue lines, which are shorter than screenplay turns; see calibration.subtitleCueBias.* and ptAdjusted.*
Subtitles have no action lines, so their conflict peaks are about half the height of screenplay peaks and only a quarter to a third of their scenes have an arc.
Scene boundaries are heuristic in every source: sluglines in MovieSum, place/time cues in fan transcripts, silences of 12 s or more in subtitles, windows of about 60 turns in stage texts.
Scene length in screenplays is the film's running time shared out by text weight (uniform pace assumed), and a reading-rate estimate for plays and TV transcripts.

notes: estVsReal: reading-rate estimate of a subtitle scene's seconds divided by its real seconds (1.0 would be exact; subtitle scenes hold speech only, so below 1 is expected where silence is long).
runtimeRatio: a film's running time divided by the reading-rate estimate of its screenplay (above 1: films run longer than text weight alone says, i.e. action, music and silence).

How to use it for pt-BR: rhythm (silenceShare, gapsOver2sPerMin, rapidShare, turnsPerMin, ellipsisShare) from pt/film/subtitle and pt/series/subtitle, which have real cue times; turn length from the same buckets only through calibration.ptAdjusted.*, because a subtitle cue is shorter than a spoken turn.

Structure and action (dirPerMin, hardActs, reversals, eventsPer10, tInciting, tClimax, aftermathShare, curves) have no pt-BR source with action lines at scale: use en/film/screenplay and the en/series/transcript children as the prior, pt/stage/play as a pt cross-check, and say so in any score that leans on them.

tInciting, tClimax and aftermathShare: read strongArc.ladders (peak 0.3+ and rise 0.15+). The hand-check found climax placement plausible in 16 of 18 such scenes and in about 60% of all scenes with an arc.
Melodrama (soap and telenovela style) exists only as en/series/transcript/melodrama (soap-opera transcripts). No pt-BR telenovela text was publicly reachable. Family drama is the drama children.

en/series/transcript pools fan transcripts with and without action lines (soap transcripts have none); read direction rates from its comedy, drama and thriller children, which are action-line transcripts.
